Tide tables published years in advance guide ships, dredging operations, and recreational boaters.
Satellite altimetry now measures sea-surface height across the globe, allowing scientists to
study how tides interact with ocean circulation and to refine models used in climate research.
Tidal energy is also being developed as a renewable resource, with turbines placed in fast-flowing
channels to extract power from the moving water, though the technology remains costly and its
environmental effects are still being studied.
In the end, ocean tides reveal how closely the Earth is bound to its neighbors in space. The same
gravity that holds the Moon in orbit lifts the oceans into bulges that sweep around the planet
each day. Those tides slow the Earth's rotation very gradually and drive the Moon slowly outward,
a process that has been unfolding for billions of years. Every rising and falling sea, from a
quiet beach to a funnel-shaped bay, is a small expression of that vast interaction. Understanding
tides therefore connects the mechanics of the solar system to the everyday experience of the
shore, and it reminds us that the ocean is always responding to forces far beyond our sight.
